# More wheel models

<!-- Generated by tools/build_more_wheels.py from more-wheels.json. Edit the JSON, then run the script. -->

Some wheel models can't be hosted in this repo. A few makers share 3D files of their own wheels but don't
allow re-uploads, and lots of people have modelled wheels under their own licences. This page lists the ones I
know about, so you can download them from the source.

If you just want one that works in Virtual Real Cockpit straight away, those are in the app under
*Get a wheel…* (and listed in [index.json](index.json)).

If you know of a model that's missing here, or a link has stopped working, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/cafealin/vrc-wheels/issues) and I'll update the list.

## No 3D files yet

I couldn't find 3D models of these makers' wheels (as of 18 October 2026): Fanatec, Thrustmaster, Logitech G, MOZA Racing, Simagic, Asetek SimSports, VRS, Cammus, Conspit, Cube Controls, Ascher Racing, Precision Sim Engineering, Gomez Sim Industries, Sim-Lab, Heusinkveld, Leo Bodnar, Sim Racing Machines. They share drawings, drilling templates or printable accessories instead. MOZA and Thrustmaster have printable accessories on Printables (for personal use), and MOZA also has a model of its R3 and R12 bases. If one of them releases files, please let me know.

## Getting one into Virtual Real Cockpit

The app loads `.glb`, `.gltf`, `.fbx`, `.obj` and `.zip` files (Wheel › model select › *Load your own model…*).

- A STEP or IGES file (CAD) needs converting first. Open it in [FreeCAD](https://www.freecad.org), which is
  free, select the parts and use File › Export › glTF. CAD models tend to have millions of triangles, so it
  helps to slim it down in Blender with a Decimate modifier until it's under 300k.
- An STL file can go through [Blender](https://www.blender.org) (also free): import it, then export it as glTF
  Binary (.glb).
- After that, line it up the way the manual's *Scan your wheel* chapter shows: hub at the centre, facing you,
  real size. The app also has *Pivot* and *Scale* settings for the last bit (Wheel › MODEL and ROTATION).

Wheel makers' names and logos belong to them, and the fan-made models aren't endorsed by the makers.
